r.정치 구도: Switzerland is a federation of 26 cantons, and a seven-member Federal Council elected by parliament runs the government together. The presidency rotates among those seven each year, so it carries little extra power. A long-standing practice shares the council seats among the four largest parties according to their vote, which blurs the line between government and opposition. In return, citizens who gather enough signatures can put laws to a referendum, so people vote several times a year. The Swiss People's Party, which campaigns for limits on immigration and distance from the EU, is the largest party in parliament. The biggest issue now is a new package of agreements with the EU signed in March 2026. After parliament debates it, a referendum could come in 2027 at the earliest.

t.why: Its permanent neutrality was recognized at the Congress of Vienna in 1815, and it has stayed out of wars since. That is why Geneva hosts the UN office in Europe, the International Committee of the Red Cross, the World Trade Organization and the World Health Organization, and why rival countries so often meet there for talks. It only joined the UN in 2002, after a referendum. It sits in the middle of the EU without being a member and reaches the European market through more than 100 separate agreements. After Russia invaded Ukraine, Switzerland adopted EU sanctions, which set off a debate at home over how far neutrality goes. In August 2025 a 39% US tariff hit it hard, and in November it agreed to a framework that lowers the rate to 15%.
t.rel: A long-neutral country that has not joined the EU but is bound to it by many agreements. Geneva hosts many UN and international bodies and often serves as a venue for mediated talks.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations began in 1963. At the 1953 armistice, Switzerland and Sweden were chosen as members of the Neutral Nations Supervisory Commission, and Swiss officers still watch over the armistice at Panmunjom. It is the longest-running peacekeeping mission of the Swiss Armed Forces. North Korea has refused to recognize the commission since 1995. In September 2006 the free trade agreement between Korea and the European Free Trade Association took effect. It was Korea's first free trade deal with European countries, and trade between the two has grown several times over since.
t.know: Switzerland has enough nuclear shelters for almost its entire population.
etext: Pharmaceuticals, led by Roche and Novartis, are the largest share of exports. Expensive, precise goods such as machinery, medical devices and watches are how the country pays some of the highest wages in the world.

Long political stability and a strong franc make it a wealth management hub where the world's rich park their assets. Geneva and Zug host firms that trade oil, grain and metals, and a large share of the world's gold passes through Swiss refineries.
Roughly two in three teenagers choose vocational training, learning on the job at a company. Skilled workers are respected without a university degree, and that system underpins Swiss manufacturing.

Whenever the world economy wobbles, the franc rises and exporters struggle. When Credit Suisse collapsed and was absorbed by UBS in 2023, the country's finance came to rest on a single giant bank. As the steep US tariffs of 2025 showed, it is an export economy easily shaken by policies set abroad.
